settings.title:
IT Migration Services That
Protect Your Data at Every Step

settings.editor: IT migration services move systems, data, users, applications or infrastructure from one environment to another.
Copying data is the smallest part of the job. A successful migration also needs discovery, dependency mapping, testing, cutover planning, validation and a rollback plan.

settings.title: How IT migration services reduce business disruption

settings.editor: Applications, users, infrastructure, data and integrations are mapped before any system moves.
Pilot tests, staged cutovers, validation checks and rollback plans lower the risk at every step.
Identity, permissions, backups, security controls and data integrity are built into the plan from day one.
Testing after the move confirms that systems, applications, users and workloads work as expected.
Covers on-premises, tenant-to-tenant, server, database, email and workload migrations.
Ongoing monitoring and support keep the new environment stable after go-live.

Example: Moving from Windows Server 2012 to Windows Server 2022.
Updated infrastructure that is supported, faster and more secure.

Data moved accurately, with permissions, structure and integrity intact.
Move databases between platforms, hosting environments or software versions.
Example: Moving from MySQL to PostgreSQL, or upgrading your current database platform.
A tested database environment with lower risk of compatibility problems and data loss.

settings.title: Moving quickly with few application changes

settings.editor: The right approach depends on your timeline, risk tolerance, technical dependencies and the condition of your current environment.
One team coordinates infrastructure, identity, networking, data, applications, storage and email
Security, access, encryption, backup and validation requirements are part of every plan
Migrations run on pilots, runbooks, rollback plans and validation checkpoints
Current environments are assessed up front, with stabilization and support after go-live
Review the source environment, target platform, dependencies, security requirements and business constraints.
Create the migration architecture, data flows, access model, timeline and cutover strategy.
Configure target systems, back up data, fix compatibility issues and complete pre-migration testing.
Move systems, users, applications or data according to the approved runbook.
Confirm data integrity, performance, user access, integrations, monitoring and security controls.
Fix post-migration issues, update documentation and hand the environment over to ongoing support.
